findings.description: The Lambda function stores a literal AWS access key ID ("AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE") and secret access key ("wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY") in its environment variables. These long-lived credentials are exposed in plaintext to anyone who can read the function configuration, are rendered into the Terraform state file, and are visible to all code running inside the function, allowing credential theft and unauthorised AWS API access. Secrets should be supplied via AWS Secrets Manager/SSM Parameter Store or the execution role instead.

The function uses runtime "nodejs12.x", an end-of-life runtime that no longer receives security patches. Running on an unmaintained runtime leaves known vulnerabilities in the language interpreter and bundled libraries unpatched and exposes the function to exploitation.
